stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly boosted in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance gain is achieved through the implementation of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent performance shows up to a 90% speed increase when benchmarked using Aider.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in the MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher output quality, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The key feature is the ability to run these AI agents locally on the user's own hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, leveraging local LLM infrastructure.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for performance optimization.
This integration specifically targets Apple Silicon hardware, leveraging Apple's native ML framework.
The feature is currently available in a preview state, indicating ongoing development and optimization.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed for local execution.
It integrates messaging apps with local AI coding agents.
The core feature emphasizes running AI entirely on the user's own device for privacy.

stories.title: Big Tech accused of stonewalling European social media researchers
stories.author: Anna Desmarais, wired.com
bullet_points: Major tech platforms (TikTok, X, Meta) are facing accusations of non-compliance.
The core issue is the alleged stonewalling of European social media researchers.
These companies are reportedly failing to provide data that is legally required under EU regulations.

stories.title: 3D-Aware VLMs with Implicit and Explicit Geometries
stories.author: Gongjie Zhang
bullet_points: Addresses a key limitation of current 2D Vision-Language Models (VLMs) in handling complex 3D spatial reasoning tasks.
Introduces VLM-IE3D, a unified framework designed to enhance 3D spatial awareness in VLMs.
Achieves this enhancement by integrating both implicit and explicit 3D geometries, utilizing novel Implicit Geometry Tokens (IGTs).

stories.title: GraphVid: Interactive Graph-Controllable Video Generation
stories.author: Ismini Lourentzou
bullet_points: GraphVid addresses the challenge of precise multi-object interaction control in video generation.
It overcomes limitations of text prompts and trajectory-based controls that struggle with scene complexity and occlusion.
The method utilizes a graph-based approach to enable flexible and precise control over multiple subjects in generated videos.

stories.title: OpenForgeRL: Train Harness-native Agents in Any Environment
stories.author: Jianfeng Gao
bullet_points: Introduces OpenForgeRL, an open-source framework designed to train complex AI agents end-to-end.
Addresses the challenge of training agents that rely on elaborate, stateful inference harnesses (like Claude Code/Codex) within open infrastructure.
Enables multi-turn reasoning and tool use for agents across diverse environments without relying solely on proprietary harness stacks.

stories.title: 3D-Aware VLMs with Implicit and Explicit Geometries
stories.author: Gongjie Zhang
bullet_points: Addresses a critical limitation in current 2D Vision-Language Models (VLMs) regarding 3D spatial understanding.
Introduces VLM-IE3D, a unified framework that integrates both implicit and explicit 3D geometries derived from RGB videos.
Employs novel Implicit Geometry Tokens (IGTs) to enhance the model's ability to capture high-level geometric priors.

stories.title: DONDO: Open w2v-BERT Speech-Recognition Base Models for African Languages
stories.author: Paul Azunre
bullet_points: Introduction of DONDO, a family of open, permissively licensed ASR base models specifically for African languages.
The models are built upon the w2v-BERT 2.0 self-supervised speech encoder and cover 27 language varieties across several African nations.
Training data primarily consists of read speech sourced from religious texts, ensuring broad and license-clear usage.

stories.title: Windowed-MTP: Removing the Full-Context Draft-KV Tax at Million-Token Context
stories.author: Alagappan Valliappan
bullet_points: The paper addresses a critical performance bottleneck in speculative decoding when using Multi-Token-Prediction (MTP) draft heads.
The issue arises because MTP draft heads incur a linear cost with context length due to full attention over the KV cache at each draft step.
The proposed 'Windowed-MTP' aims to mitigate this 'Full-Context Draft-KV Tax' to enable efficient use of MTP in models with million-token context windows.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces significant performance improvements.
Enhanced GGUF model compatibility is now available via llama.cpp integration.
The update broadens model support across various hardware, augmenting the MLX engine on Apple silicon.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for advanced AI features within Claude Code.
The new capabilities include the implementation of subagents for more complex task decomposition.
Web search functionality has been added, enhancing the model's ability to access real-time information.

stories.title: SpaceX eyes tower catch for next Starship after auspicious end to 13th flight
stories.author: Stephen Clark
bullet_points: SpaceX plans to attempt a tower catch for the next Starship flight.
This follows a successful conclusion to the 13th Starship flight.
The maneuver indicates continued development and iteration on Starship recovery procedures.

stories.title: Anthropic's Opus 5 is about token efficiency, not a capability leap
stories.author: Samuel Axon
bullet_points: Anthropic's Opus 5 update emphasizes token efficiency over massive capability gains.
The article suggests that current, less expensive AI models are often sufficient for practical use cases.
This points to a trend where efficiency and cost-effectiveness are becoming as important as raw performance in LLM development.

stories.title: Beyond Sufficiency: Time Series Explanation with Counterfactual Necessity
stories.author: Weiru Liu
bullet_points: Introduces TimePNS, a new framework for time-series explanation.
Addresses a limitation in existing methods by moving beyond mere 'sufficiency' to incorporate 'necessity' in explanations.
Aims to prevent spurious subsequences from being over-weighted when explaining black-box time-series classifiers.

stories.title: Beyond Sycophancy: Structured Resistance and Compliance in LLM Moral Reasoning
stories.author: Bernard Koch
bullet_points: The research addresses the limitation of simply reducing 'sycophancy' in LLMs for moral reasoning.
It proposes that socially calibrated LLMs must learn to distinguish between incorporating external perspectives and maintaining independent moral judgment.
The study identifies three structured dimensions governing how models revise their judgments based on external input.

stories.title: MIRROR: Learning from the Other View for Multi-Modal Reasoning
stories.author: Xuezhe Ma
bullet_points: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) show inconsistent reasoning capabilities across different input modalities (text vs. diagrams).
The study highlights that different views (e.g., text only, diagram only, combined) can elicit different behaviors in VLMs.
The research proposes that these view-dependent inconsistencies suggest that different modalities expose complementary reasoning paths.

stories.title: Expanding Flow Maps
stories.author: Pranam Chatterjee
bullet_points: Introduces Expanding Generative Flows (EFlows) to address limitations in existing flow-based generative models.
EFlows allow for generation across distributions of increasing dimensionality by augmenting the state with conditional noise.
This research aims to overcome constraints related to fixed dimensions or fixed sequence lengths in current generative models.

stories.title: Beyond Sufficiency: Time Series Explanation with Counterfactual Necessity
stories.author: Weiru Liu
bullet_points: Introduces TimePNS, a new framework for explaining time-series classifiers.
Addresses a limitation in current methods by requiring explanations to be not just sufficient, but also necessary for the prediction.
Draws inspiration from Pearl's counterfactual notions to identify essential subsequences in time-series data.

stories.title: Graph Learning on Ensembles of Cyclic Peptides: An Investigation of Molecular Ensemble Modeling
stories.author: Maxim Secor
bullet_points: Introduces EnsembleEGNN, a foundation model designed to handle molecular conformational ensembles rather than single structures.
The model utilizes Equivariant Graph Neural Networks (EGNNs) to encode individual conformers, followed by a Set Attention Block for ensemble pooling.
It is pre-trained on CREMP, a dataset specifically focused on cyclic peptide ensembles, addressing a gap in molecular property prediction.

stories.title: MIRROR: Learning from the Other View for Multi-Modal Reasoning
stories.author: Xuezhe Ma
bullet_points: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) show inconsistent reasoning capabilities across different input modalities (text vs. visual diagrams).
The study suggests that different views (text, diagram, combined) expose complementary, yet sometimes conflicting, reasoning pathways in VLMs.
The research introduces 'MIRROR' to address this multi-modal reasoning gap, aiming to leverage insights from different views.

stories.title: X$^3$-OPD: Distilling Reasoning into Large Audio-Language Models via On-Policy Alignment
stories.author: Tao Jin
bullet_points: Addresses the gap in deep logical reasoning for large audio-language models compared to text-based LLMs.
Introduces X$^3$-OPD, a cross-modal on-policy distillation framework.
The framework transfers reasoning capabilities from a powerful text teacher model to an audio-language student model.

stories.title: The Boundaries of Automation: A Theory of Persistent Human Participation
stories.author: Iryna Gurevych
bullet_points: The paper challenges the prevailing assumption that human involvement in AI is solely due to current system limitations.
It shifts the focus from 'how far automation can extend' to identifying the conceptual limits of automation.
The research posits that human participation may remain necessary even when AI systems achieve high levels of capability.

stories.title: MedGame: Storytelling Gamification Empowered by Large Language Models for Medical Education
stories.author: Qi Dou
bullet_points: Introduces MedGame, a framework that uses LLMs to transform static clinical cases into interactive, decision-centered storytelling games for medical education.
Addresses a limitation in current LLM medical education tools, which often only support localized interactions like Q&A, rather than full case trajectory management.
Employs a dual-engine design, including a Medical Narrative Designer, to synthesize case-grounded clinical stories.

stories.title: OpenForgeRL: Train Harness-native Agents in Any Environment
stories.author: Jianfeng Gao
bullet_points: Introduces OpenForgeRL, an open-source framework designed to train AI agents end-to-end.
Addresses the difficulty of training agents when relying on complex, proprietary inference harnesses (like Claude Code/Codex).
Enables training in diverse environments by natively supporting stateful, multi-process harness inference.

stories.title: GS-Agent: Creating 4D Physical Worlds With Generative Simulation
stories.author: Chuang Gan
bullet_points: The research focuses on generating dynamic and physically realistic 4D worlds from natural language descriptions.
It addresses the limitations of traditional computer graphics, which require extensive manual effort for creation.
The core challenge being tackled is ensuring physical plausibility and controllability in generative simulation models.

stories.title: Artificial Epanorthosis: Why large language models overuse a classical rhetorical figure, and how to mitigate it
stories.author: Federico Boggia
bullet_points: LLMs exhibit a systematic overuse of 'epanorthosis,' a classical rhetorical self-correction figure.
The overuse is attributed to training data rich in promotional prose and RLHF tuning that favors confident phrasing.
The paper suggests the left-to-right nature of LLM generation contributes to this rhetorical pattern.

stories.title: What, Where, and How: Disentangling the Roles of Task, Language, and Model in Code Model Representations
stories.author: Piotr Wilam
bullet_points: The research investigates how different independently trained code language models (Qwen2.5-Coder and DeepSeek-Coder) represent grammatical concepts across two languages (Python and Rust).
The study uses a 2x2 design to disentangle the influence of the specific task, the programming language, and the underlying model architecture on code representation.
The findings suggest that the representation of grammatical concepts is not uniform across all combinations of task, language, and model.

stories.title: Agentic coding without the cloud: evaluating open-weight large language models on longitudinal data preparation tasks
stories.author: David Bann
bullet_points: Addresses the privacy constraint of using cloud-based LLMs for sensitive data tasks.
Proposes using locally deployable, open-weight LLMs as a privacy-preserving alternative.
Introduces an open-source framework to evaluate the performance of AI agents on data preparation tasks.

stories.title: Tracing a multi-agent LLM system: otel-swarm and a SigNoz dashboard pack
stories.author: himanshu_748
bullet_points: Addresses the complexity of debugging multi-agent Large Language Model (LLM) systems.
Introduces 'otel-swarm' as a tool for tracing these complex LLM interactions.
Utilizes a SigNoz dashboard pack for visualizing and monitoring the multi-agent workflow.

stories.title: #Neo4j vs pgvector vs MongoDB vs Milvus vs Pinecone vs FAISS: The Complete Vector Database Guide for 2026
stories.author: nikhil_ramank_152ca48266
bullet_points: The article addresses the critical decision-making process for selecting a vector database for RAG systems.
It provides a comparative guide covering major players like Neo4j, pgvector, MongoDB, Milvus, Pinecone, and FAISS.
The focus on '2026' suggests forward-looking analysis on evolving industry standards in AI/ML infrastructure.

stories.title: I reverse-engineered Claude's undocumented Design API so a file sync wouldn't cost 665k tokens
stories.author: somework
bullet_points: The article details the reverse-engineering of Claude's undocumented Design API.
The motivation was to avoid extremely high token costs (665k tokens) associated with a file synchronization task.
It serves as a case study in 'protocol archaeology' and the challenges of working with undocumented APIs.

stories.title: Image-layer prompt injection: measuring a defense across 108,015 samples
stories.author: rustycoder31
bullet_points: The article addresses a specific vulnerability: image-layer prompt injection.
It focuses on measuring the effectiveness of existing prompt injection defenses.
The research tests these defenses across a large dataset of 108,015 samples.

stories.title: Tracing Voice AI is Hard: How I Instrumented Streaming LLMs with OpenTelemetry and SigNoz
stories.author: jay9122
bullet_points: Addresses a common real-world problem in Voice AI: latency and performance tracking.
Details the technical solution using OpenTelemetry and SigNoz for instrumentation.
Focuses on practical application with streaming LLMs (specifically mentioning Groq).

stories.title: The Delegate Pattern: Run Claude Code + Codex + Gemini in Parallel — Zero-Cost Rate Limit Bypass for Multi-Agent AI
stories.author: m_t_bbe0d7e2206ba4769563b
bullet_points: Proposes a 'Delegate Pattern' to run multiple LLMs (Claude, Codex, Gemini) concurrently.
The primary goal is to mitigate frequent service interruptions ('AI stops') experienced during large-scale AI operations.
Claims the pattern offers a 'Zero-Cost Rate Limit Bypass' for multi-agent AI workflows.
